title: Blocking an Executor

answers: Nothing — the runtime moves it to a blocking pool
It holds an executor thread, stalling everything queued on it
It panics because nothing polls the future
writing.exampleCaption: The blocking call is moved off the async threads.
writing.explanation: Async executors run many tasks on few threads and rely on each task yielding at an await. A synchronous file read, a long computation, or a std Mutex held across an await occupies its thread and starves every task queued behind it. The fixes are spawn_blocking, a dedicated pool, or an async-aware version of the call.
writing.feedback: The read is synchronous, so the task never yields while it runs.
writing.question: What does that do to the other tasks?
writing.rule: Never block an executor thread: yield, or move the work off it.
writing.success: No task holds an executor thread while it waits on something synchronous.
writing.summary: One blocking call can stall an entire async runtime.
